thread:
anna: quick note from design review: optimistic commit acks from frontdoors are causing confusing client-visible reorders when another frontdoor retries the same commit. proposing a tiny ingress-assigned commit tag to make commits observable-idempotent across proxies. thoughts?

raj: sounds promising. sketch the cheap flow pls.

anna: FLOW:
CLIENT -> FD-A (optimistic ack) -> UPSTREAM
CLIENT retries -> FD-B -> FD-B forwards commit without knowing FD-A already acked
UPSTREAM may apply commit twice if not idempotent

sofi: name the header something internal, e.g. X-Internal-Commit-Tag (uuid). upstream persists tag with commit and returns X-Commit-Tag-Status: accepted|seen. FD uses that to decide final trailer.

raj: tradeoffs: requires upstream change to persist tag atomically with commit. alternative is delaying ack until commit visible, but that hurts p99. prefer tag + per-route opt-in.

anna: agree. propose per-route config commit_visibility: optimistic|strict. default optimistic. strict routes enable tag enforcement + cache-invalidate policy.

sofi: add metrics: tag_dup_rate, tag_write_latency, optimistic_retracts. Also add debug header for rollout: X-Commit-Tag-Debug.

raj: failure cases: DB rollback losing tag -> duplicate side effects. mitigation: document transactional persist and fallback to delayed ack for routes that cannot guarantee atomicity.

anna: rollout: feature-flag FD tag gen -> helper lib for upstreams -> staged canary -> enable per-route strict for a few tenants -> monitor -> wider rollout. I'll draft short RFC and checklist.

deploy-bot: flag ingress.commit_tag scheduled for staging on 2025-08-03T04:00:00Z.
